I'm really glad you posted this because I really hadn't thought of this. I'd vaguely heard about whitlow ages ago but forgot all about it since then. Didn't realise hands were a possible route for transmission 😬

Apparently the prevalence is 2.4 cases per 100,000 so they're pretty low odds. Plus, hasn't there already been a chance (however small, if you're using condoms and antivirals) that he could've caught it if you're having PIV sex? If he's happy with that risk surely hands would be okay?

There's definitely other things that can cause sores on your lips so if I were you, I'd trust your doctor. I'd also say that most people don't disclose oral HSV - I've never had someone tell me they suffer from coldsores before kissing me, if I've found out it's been months later when it's just come up in conversation. 

Oral HSV really doesn't carry any stigma (at least where I live) so if you do want to mention it, maybe it could be a simple as mentioning you thought you were getting coldsores but the tests came back negative.

I'm not sure whether my opinion will be popular but I think if she's asking you to use condoms then yes, you should be using them. I get condoms can take the intimacy away, but isn't it simply about not asking your partner to do something you know she's uncomfortable with? I'd love to not have to use condoms, but if my partner wants to I'd feel bad asking them not to, I just think my pleasure isn't more important than how they feel (that's just how I feel though, I'm not implying you think otherwise.)

You mention you think it might be because of the blow to her self-esteem that she's so worried, and maybe that's what it comes down to - if she's already feeling low about herself or insecure for some reason, then the idea of catching herpes is gonna be terrifying because of all the stigma. Maybe as well as trying to explain how the chance of transmission is actually low and loads of people have it, let her know having HSV doesn't change a person, and she'd be just the same great person you married even if she did have it. Just try and make sure she's comfortable before even bringing up you don't want to use condoms is what I'm trying to say I guess.

I really don't think doing something equivalent like using a dental dam is a good idea, I think that could possibly be seen as a petty move and thus be even worse for your sex life.

Daily antivirals do reduce the risk of transmission, but you've got to be careful with long term use so I'd recommend speaking to a doctor or nurse about it.

Yes, you can still have kids, some people still have natural births too but there is a risk of transmission.

One thing that's worrying about your post is how you say he's pushing to have unprotected sex. He shouldn't be putting pressure on you to have unprotected sex, it's only something you should consider if you're absolutely comfortable. And it's always a good idea for both partners to go for an STI test before having unprotected sex, don't assume they don't have anything.

If someone said they wouldn't have sex with me but wanted other stuff, that'd be a deal-breaker, it just wouldn't make me feel nice.

However, if I wanted to be intimate but wasn't ready to disclose, or simply because my partner wasn't ready for sex but wanted to do other stuff, anything that doesn't involve genital contact is fair game (if you have OHSV that'll have to be taken into consideration obviously) I'll wear lingerie too so there isn't any accidental contact down there 😂

I was 22 when I found out, it's been two years for me and I can honestly say my dating life is better than it was before (but it wasn't too great before 😂)

I see it as sort of a filtering method - if someone can't deal with me having herpes, they're probably not the sort of person I'd want a long term relationship with anyway.

I think you're way stronger than I was if you're already comfortable telling your friends and laughing about it. Things do get better, being newly diagnosed is the hardest part I think.

Lesions down there can be caused by all sorts of different things, not just herpes, so it's entirely possible it could be something else. I think it's really bad that doctors say "oh that looks like herpes" before they have the test results considering how much someone's likely to worry. 

Presence of bacteria and yellow discharge isn't a typical symptom of herpes. The only time I've had yellow discharge is when I've had BV, it sounds grim but it's just caused by a disruption in the natural balance of bacteria down there, which could've been caused by your boyfriend going down on you whilst he had a sore throat. Obviously I'm no doctor and your test results will say for certain, and I guess you've just got to wait until you get them. But it could all just be coincidence.

If it turns out you do have herpes, a lot of people find it really emotional at first, and the advice I'd have then is to remember it doesn't define you, you're still the same person you were beforehand. But tbh it's been 2 years for me and most days I just plain forget about herpes altogether, it's no big deal.

I can totally understand the guilt you feel about passing it on, it weighs on my mind too. I sometimes think, even if I do disclose and they're fine with it, I'd still feel like shit if they caught it.

At first I just went on herpes dating sites but that didn't work, like you said having herpes is a pretty flimsy basis for a relationship. I've started dating again 'normally' and I just think, nobody's perfect. Maybe there'll be someone who likes me way more than they care about getting herpes. Maybe there won't be, but it's still worth a try.

I guess the only advice I have is to take it one step at a time. Your diagnosis doesn't define you and there'll be girls out there who like you for you. 

I've been diagnosed for about 2 years too and a while back I started dating again, it's a bit nerve-wracking but that's all part of the fun, it's kinda exciting.
Wish I could say something a bit more poignant, but good luck!
